items.title: Toyota and Nvidia expand partnership to develop AI for vehicles, factories and cities
items.summary: Toyota and Nvidia expanded their partnership to develop physical AI technologies across vehicles, factories, and cities. This collaboration focuses on deploying Nvidia's computing, AI software, and simulation technologies in various business areas. Applications include developing next-generation driver-assistance systems, accelerating software engineering with AI coding assistants, and creating digital twins for factory simulations. Furthermore, the partnership is being applied to urban mobility through vision-language models for traffic analysis. The goal is to build the AI infrastructure for more autonomous vehicles, intelligent manufacturing, and responsive urban environments.

The partnership involves utilizing Nvidia's technologies to develop next-generation driver-assistance systems, accelerate software engineering through AI coding assistants, and create digital twins for factory simulations. Additionally, the collaboration is being applied to urban mobility by using vision-language models for complex traffic analysis. This work aims to establish the necessary AI infrastructure for autonomous vehicles, intelligent manufacturing, and responsive city environments. The development signals a tangible progression toward integrating advanced artificial intelligence into physical world systems.

items.title: Nvidia and Hugging Face expand LeRobot with new open robotics AI tools
items.summary: Nvidia and Hugging Face expanded their collaboration to integrate new AI models and robotics frameworks into the open-source LeRobot platform. This expansion includes integrating Nvidia Isaac GR00T 1.7 and the Isaac Teleop framework for standardized data collection, training, and deployment workflows. Future plans involve incorporating Nvidia Cosmos 3 to allow access to world foundation models for synthetic data generation and policy development. The partnership aims to make advanced physical AI technologies more accessible to the broader robotics community. These additions leverage existing Nvidia resources and increase access for both AI and robotics developers.

Future plans include integrating Nvidia Cosmos 3 to provide access to world foundation models for synthetic data generation and policy development within the system. This collaboration aims to increase accessibility to advanced physical AI technologies for the broader robotics community by leveraging existing Nvidia resources. The integration is expected to accelerate the development of open-source robotics AI tools.

The goal is to create a collaborative control platform connecting digital systems with robots and physical equipment. This initiative aims to address challenges like labor shortages and aging workforces through the adoption of physical AI. The partnership will develop an open platform integrating AI, robotics, simulation, and data analysis technologies for interoperability and security. Fujitsu will utilize Nvidia's foundation models and Omniverse libraries to enhance robot learning and simulation workflows.

items.title: Weave Robotics launches Isaac, its first mobile humanoid robot
items.summary: Weave Robotics launched Isaac 1, a wheeled humanoid robot designed for household chores like folding laundry and tidying rooms. This consumer robot features a friendly, soft exterior, adjustable height, and autonomous navigation capabilities. It can be controlled remotely via an app and operates on an eight-hour battery with a two-hour recharge time. A unique feature includes shutters on the head cameras to indicate when the robot is working, and privacy screens for charging. Isaac 1 is positioned as an affordable entry into home robotics through purchase or subscription models.

items.title: mimic Robotics unveils full-stack platform for dexterous robot manipulation
items.summary: mimic Robotics introduced a full-stack platform featuring the mimic hand M1, a tendon-driven robotic hand, and the mimic wearable U1 exoskeleton. This system is designed to advance general-purpose dexterous manipulation for industrial robots by collecting high-quality training data. The design maintains a human hand morphology across hardware, data collection, and model training to avoid cross-embodiment gaps. The hardware includes force sensing, high backdrivability, and tactile sensors, supported by custom middleware to reduce latency. Ultimately, the platform aims to create a general-purpose robotics foundation model for physical AI.

items.title: Kimi K3 launch shifts AI focus to efficiency stack
items.summary: The Kimi K3 launch prompted a reassessment of AI development, shifting the focus from raw compute to the efficiency stack. K3 demonstrated strong performance in coding and frontend tasks, challenging the "compute moat" thesis with advancements in methods like MoE routing and data curation. Technical interest focused on K3's use of Kimi Delta Attention for faster and cheaper context processing. The value is now seen moving toward orchestration, memory architectures, and workflow scaffolding rather than just base model access. Benchmarks indicate K3 achieved frontier-level results in coding agents and frontend evaluation.

Benchmarks indicated that K3 achieved frontier-level results in coding agents and frontend evaluations by focusing computational resources efficiently. items.title: Agility Robotics opens new Fremont facility to accelerate physical AI development

items.summary: Automation investment success hinges on the software layer, with Warehouse Execution Systems acting as the "brain" connecting hardware and people for unified control. Software-first strategies are replacing hardware-led approaches to ensure flexibility and adaptability in evolving operational needs. Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) have become core infrastructure, supported by accessible models like Robotics-as-a-Service. Predictive operations driven by AI require a strong orchestration platform for real-time visibility across all systems and data. Future success in automation will depend on creating hardware-agnostic software platforms that allow for seamless, flexible growth.

items.title: Interview with Scott Zerkle of Panasonic Connect: ‘AI is only as good as the data it receives’
items.summary: AI's greatest current value in electronics manufacturing is predictive maintenance and defect detection, supporting workers rather than replacing them. The future of smart manufacturing involves connecting data across machines, materials, and processes to allow factories to learn and improve from their production history. Component miniaturization necessitates highly precise printing and placement that must adapt in real-time. Automation helps balance quality, throughput, and resilience by monitoring the 5Ms (human, machine, material, method, measurement). The major upcoming shift will be the convergence of AI, sensing, and automation to create interconnected, self-optimizing manufacturing ecosystems.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Interview with Scott Zerkle of Panasonic Connect: ‘AI is only as good as the data it receives’". This report details the current application and future trajectory of artificial intelligence within electronics manufacturing, highlighting that AI's primary value currently lies in predictive maintenance and defect detection supporting human workers. The future of smart manufacturing involves integrating data from machines, materials, and processes to allow factories to learn and improve based on production history. Component miniaturization demands highly precise printing and placement that must adapt in real time. Automation assists in balancing quality, throughput, and resilience by monitoring the five Ms of manufacturing: human, machine, material, method, and measurement. The major upcoming shift involves the convergence of artificial intelligence, sensing, and automation to form interconnected, self-optimizing manufacturing ecosystems. This development signals a move toward fully integrated, adaptive factory environments driven by comprehensive data streams.

items.title: Aetina adds support for Nvidia Jetson T3000 and T2000 AI modules
items.summary: Aetina plans to expand its portfolio by supporting the new Nvidia Jetson T3000 and T2000 AI modules for robotics and industrial edge AI. These modules will be integrated into Aetina's upcoming DeviceEdge AIE-KT and AIE-PT fan-based and fanless systems, respectively. The Jetson T3000 offers up to 865 FP4 TFLOPS at 70W, while the T2000 provides up to 400 FP4 TFLOPS for applications like autonomous robots. Aetina's hardware families will enable customers to scale robotics projects from development to production. Nvidia anticipates module availability in the first quarter of 2027 and full support for the AI software ecosystem.

Aetina intends to integrate these modules into its upcoming DeviceEdge AIE-KT and AIE-PT fan-based and fanless systems, respectively. The Jetson T3000 module offers up to 865 FP4 TFLOPS at a power consumption of 70 watts, while the T2000 provides up to 400 FP4 TFLOPS suitable for applications such as autonomous robots. Nvidia forecasts module availability in the first quarter of 2027 along with full support for the associated AI software ecosystem.
